title: Active learning finds a trace additive for ultrafast-charging sodium metal batteries
summary: An active-learning framework based on Gaussian process regression, guided by physicochemical descriptors, identified sodium chlorodifluoroacetate (NaCDFA) as a trace-level (0.02 M) additive that promotes PF6- anion decomposition and builds a NaF-rich interphase. The Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cell cycled over 50,000 cycles at 200 C, and performance was retained with high-mass-loading cathodes and limited-sodium or anode-free designs. One additive is reported, and the machine-learning role is the screening step.
ai_technology: Gaussian process regression active learning over physicochemical descriptors to select an electrolyte additive

evidence.tested: Cell cycling, in situ characterization and calculations on Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells with the additive.
evidence.unknown: Generality beyond one additive and long-term performance in practical cells; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Active learning identified the NaCDFA additive.
